name: Managed IT support and cybersecurity firms

problems.words: Clients WhatsApp the engineer directly and the ticket never gets logged
quick_ideas: Give every client one support number and tell them once, so requests stop landing on personal phones
Ask engineers to forward this week's direct requests to it, so you see the real volume.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp and email ticket intake that logs every request with client, priority and SLA timer, and replies with a reference number.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many AMC clients do you support?
problems.free_stops: the intake flow and priority rules are set out in the solution document.

problems.words: We breach SLAs and only know when the client complains
quick_ideas: Write down once the response times you promised each client, so everyone knows them
Check open tickets against those times today, so near-breaches get handled.

workzap_build.text: an SLA screen showing tickets close to breach by client and engineer, with alerts before the time runs out.

problems.free_stops: alert thresholds per contract are kept for the solution document.

problems.words: Fixed AMC clients use us far more than they pay for
quick_ideas: Count last month's tickets and visits per client once, so heavy users show
Put that next to each contract once, so you have facts for renewals.

workzap_build.text: usage against contract allowance per client, rolled into a contract profitability view each month.

problems.free_stops: how effort is measured against each contract is worked out in the solution document.

problems.words: I don't know where field engineers are or how many visits they did
quick_ideas: Ask engineers to send a short end-of-day list of visits for one week, so you get a first picture
Plan tomorrow's visits on one sheet, so assignments are clear.

workzap_build.text: a field visit app with assigned jobs, site check-in and check-out, work notes and photos, and client sign-off.

problems.free_stops: the visit flow and sign-off steps are set out in the solution document.

problems.words: Licence renewals get missed and the client's service stops
quick_ideas: List every licence and subscription renewal for the next three months once, so nothing comes as a surprise
Tell the affected clients early, so approvals are in time.

workzap_build.text: a renewal calendar with reminders to the team and the client at set intervals before each date.

problems.free_stops: reminder timings and the client approval flow are kept for the solution document.

problems.words: We pay the vendor for licences before the client pays us
quick_ideas: List renewals you've paid for but not yet collected, so the gap is clear
Invoice upcoming renewals earlier this time, so money comes in before you pay out.

workzap_build.text: receivables per client linked to renewal dates, with invoices raised ahead of vendor payments and reminders.

problems.free_stops: the invoicing timeline is set out in the solution document.

problems.words: Invoices for extra work go out late or not at all
quick_ideas: Go through last month's tickets once for out-of-scope work, so unbilled jobs show
Invoice those this week, so the money is recovered.

workzap_build.text: an out-of-scope work log that drafts invoices automatically when a job is closed.

problems.free_stops: how out-of-scope work is identified is worked out in the solution document.

problems.words: Client documentation is in one senior engineer's head
quick_ideas: Ask the senior engineer to write a one-page overview for your biggest client, kept free of passwords, so the basics are shared
Name a second engineer per key client, so there's backup.

workzap_build.text: a client documentation vault with structure and asset lists (not credentials in plain view), access controls and change history.

problems.free_stops: the vault structure and access rules are kept for the solution document.

problems.words: Backup checks are supposed to be done monthly but aren't
quick_ideas: List which clients' checks are due and who owns each, so responsibility is clear
Do one round of overdue checks this week, so the backlog clears.

workzap_build.text: recurring maintenance checklists with completion tracked by client and engineer, and overdue items flagged.

problems.free_stops: the checklist contents and schedule are designed in the solution document.

problems.words: Spare parts and stock in our store don't match records
quick_ideas: Do one full count of the store, so you have a true starting figure
Start signing parts out to engineers, so movements are recorded.

workzap_build.text: a store and spare parts register with issue and return to engineers and alerts when items run low.

problems.free_stops: the issue and return routine is set out in the solution document.

never_say: Any technical security guidance or incident-response instructions; for a live breach, suggest following their incident process and contacting the relevant authorities.
Anything involving unauthorised access, cracking licences, hidden monitoring of employees or concealing a breach.
That systems will be secure or that uptime is guaranteed.
Requests for passwords, admin credentials, network diagrams, vulnerability details or client data.

sample_reply.person: Half our AMC clients just WhatsApp my engineers directly and nothing gets logged. How do we fix this?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this is very fixable, and you can start this week. 1) Give every client one support number and tell them about it once, so requests stop landing on personal phones. 2) Ask engineers to forward this week's direct messages to that number, so you see the real workload. Workzap can do this automatically for you: every WhatsApp or email request logged as a ticket with an SLA timer and a reference number sent back. Would you like me to put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
